episodes.206021: A very unstable environment was in place over western and central North Dakota which combined with very strong deep layer shear to produce widespread severe thunderstorm wind gusts along with some large hail over western and central North Dakota. To start the episode, a pair of upper level short-wave troughs approached North Dakota from Montana. The first trough had limited storm develop due to a capped atmosphere, though one storm did strengthen enough to produce one-inch diameter hail over Rolette County. Storms primarily developed as the second trough approached. Initially, storms produced a mix of large hail and strong wind gusts, but as the episode evolved and the storms moved east, very strong wind gusts became the primary concern by late evening. Significant damage occurred at multiple locations, with the two most notable events occurring in Stutsman County. In Jamestown, significant damage occurred over the southern part of the city, primarily to trees. Damage also occurred to some homes and buildings. To the north of Courtenay, a farm suffered significant damage to buildings and grain handling equipment. Winds at both locations were estimated at 100 mph, with both locations also suffering significant damage during the June 20, 2025 derecho event.
episodes.206294: An embedded wave within more broad troughing digging into the Pacific Northwest moved across the region late night August 6 into August 7. Elevated instability increased as showers and thunderstorms moved eastward from Central Montana toward Fergus county. As these thunderstorms continued to balloon and cross Lewistown Divide, they became severe, producing a wide swath of gusts in excess of 55 mph, including a peak gust of 71 mph just east of Lewistown Divide.||Later in the day ample instability and shear developed across Fergus county again to result in an instance of large hail near Grass Range.
episodes.206593: Slow moving thunderstorms produced isolated areas of flash flooding.
episodes.206607: Late afternoon storms under easterly flow sea breeze regime produce lightning strikes that injure one person near Lealman in Pinellas County, cause an apartment fire near Holiday in Pasco County, and produce a gustnado near Pinellas Park in Pinellas County.
episodes.206608: Early evening storms under easterly flow sea breeze regime produce gusty marine winds over Tampa Bay waters.
episodes.206749: Heavy thunderstorm rainfall of 2 to 4 inches on saturated soils resulted in flooding of the North Fork Whetstone River near Milbank late on the evening of August 6th.
episodes.206812: Repeated heavy rainfall from slow-moving thunderstorms over the Kendale Lakes area of Miami-Dade County produced 2 to 3 inches of accumulated rainfall which led to street flooding.
episodes.206813: Thunderstorms that moved into the Atlantic waters on the afternoon of August 7, 2025 produced waterspouts and strong wind gusts off the Miami-Dade County coast.
episodes.207058: Storms developed along the Black Hills just to the west and south of Sturgis during the rally. A storm coming off the Black Hills was able to produce a funnel cloud on the west side of Rapid City that had a lot of exposure.
episodes.207155: Diurnal heating and local effects promoted afternoon showers and t-storms which, according to reports, caused a small stream in Aguada to overflow and result in a sector of PR-115 being impassable.
episodes.207197: Two deep thunderstorm cells in the coastal waters off southwest Florida produced outflow boundaries which focused new thunderstorm development. Several gale-force wind gusts occurred as the thunderstorms moved south-southwest from the Gulf side to oceanside of the Lower Florida Keys.
episodes.207229: A typical summertime pattern was in place across the region, with intense daytime heating and abundant low-level moisture leading to the development of numerous afternoon thunderstorms. The storms were primarily outflow-driven, producing locally strong and gusty winds. One storm produced a waterspout that developed along its outflow boundary over the coastal waters. Another storm generated a severe marine wind gust that was recorded at Lakefront Airport. No damage or injuries were reported.
episodes.207230: A typical summertime pattern was in place across the region, with intense daytime heating and abundant low-level moisture leading to the development of numerous afternoon thunderstorms. The storms were primarily outflow-driven, producing locally strong and gusty winds. A couple storms reached severe limits, knocking down trees and powerlines.
episodes.207306: Many thunderstorms occurred across southeast MT, producing gusts up to 79 mph and hail sizes up to 1.75 inches. This event caused medium sized tree limbs to be snapped off, and caused extensive damage around Billings.
episodes.207543: Iowa was on the edge of a deep thermal ridge. Several weak embedded waves moved across, aiding in thunderstorms development as the interacted with the low level jet through the early morning. These early morning storms did remain sub severe, but produced heavy rain that continued through midday. Training storms across southern Iowa result in an area of five to seven plus inches of rain, but no flash flooding occurred there. Three plus inches of rain occurred in parts of Clarke, Decatur, and Wayne counties with culverts and secondary roads washed out in flash flooding. A single storm in southern Iowa strengthened as it was preparing to cross the border into Missouri. While it did not produce widespread severe damage, it did produce a microburst over the small town of Lineville, IA. A review of damage photos and drone footage provided by the Emergency Manager are consistent with straight line or microburst winds estimated of up to 90 mph. The damage footprint impacted outbuildings on the north end of Lineville and grain bins in south Lineville (a roughly 1 mile swath); as well as damage to trees and destruction of the fire station damage in between. The damage pattern in-town and in cornfields upstream did not reveal a focused track; instead a more erratic and fanning out pattern typical of severe straight line winds.
episodes.208186: Hot and very humid air mass in place created an unstable environment, which, in the presence of the Lake Huron lake breeze and a subtle stationary boundary stretching from the Keweenaw Peninsula to northern Lake Huron, was able to support development of scattered strong to severe storms across parts of northeast Lower Michigan during the late afternoon on the 7th, resulting in primarily large hail reports.
